sentences.latin: Pater filio suo librum bonum dat.
sentences.english: The father gives his own son a good book.
The big book is carried by the boy.

sentences.latin: Servi domino suo donum magnum dant.
sentences.english: The servants give their master a large gift.
The holy temple is opened.
The big dog guards the long road.
The girl is called by her own brother.
The teacher says many words to the boys.

sentences.latin: Liber meus a sorore mea servatur.
sentences.english: My book is protected by my sister.
The sailor makes for the small island.
Good gifts are prepared by the servants.
The brave man loves the beautiful woman.
The woman is loved by the brave man.
The boy believes the loyal sailor.
The soldiers are ruled by the strong king.
The servants guard their own fields.
The king commands the brave soldiers.
The great city is guarded by the men.

sentences.latin: Mater filiae suae donum parvum dat.
sentences.english: The mother gives her own daughter a small gift.

sentences.latin: Libri mei a fratribus meis habentur.
sentences.english: My books are possessed by my brothers.
The just king reigns.
The brother says sweet words to the sister.

sentences.latin: Agri nostri a servis multis parantur.
sentences.english: Our fields are prepared by many servants.
The boy sees the small dog.
The boy answers his own father.
The great gate is opened by the farmer.
